impact: ccusageFetchedAt cannot honestly be populated 'from the invocation': ccusage embeds pricing data at build time and its output provides no pricing-fetch timestamp, so daemon invocation time proves only when ccusage ran. T-010 also requires the field to be a non-empty explicit instant, so the promised absence representation is unavailable for this scalar. ADDRESSED as far as T-011 can and otherwise DEFERRED into ISS-075, same root cause. The plan states there is no honest value available under the current schema, that this is a schema question rather than an implementation choice (the field wants a discriminated value such as {kind:'embedded', ccusageVersion, pricingRevision} or {kind:'unknown'}), and that the bootstrap generation is provisional in this one documented field — which is why the whole generation carries refreshTier='bootstrap' rather than passing as an ordinary publish.
resolution:
Resolved 2026-08-05 by commit 9524902 (ticket T-026), which landed N-007 decision 2: Provenance.ccusageFetchedAt is renamed to ccusageInvokedAt.

WHY THIS ACTUALLY CLOSES IT, not merely renames around it. The issue's defect was that no caller could honestly populate a field meaning "when pricing was fetched": ccusage embeds pricing at build time and its output reports no such timestamp, so the daemon's invocation time proves only when ccusage RAN. The field now asks for exactly that provable fact. The witness is concrete, as RULES.md L-006 requires: T-011's writer reads its own clock immediately before spawning ccusage. The discriminated {kind:"embedded"|"unknown"} value this issue proposed was NOT adopted and is not needed — no required field asks for pricing recency any more, so the schema makes no pricing-recency claim at all. That is honest by omission rather than by a placeholder.

VERIFIED IN THE TREE, not assumed: src/snapshot/types.ts:301 declares ccusageInvokedAt with the rationale comment at :294-300; src/snapshot/store.ts:960 carries it in PROVENANCE_KEYS; :1077 requires it non-empty; :1083 requires an explicit-offset instant. No ccusageFetchedAt remains in src/ or tests-ts/ apart from the deliberate rename-history note at types.ts:298. The bootstrap publish this issue blocked was reproduced end-to-end against the built store: an honest candidate publishes and readSnapshot returns ok; omitting the field throws SnapshotStoreResetError (exact-key violation); the old key throws the same.

RESIDUAL RECORDED SO IT IS NOT LOST: the SIBLING field ccusageVersion is a required non-empty string that NOTHING in src/ currently produces at all (the only hits are the declaration at types.ts:293 and the two key lists at store.ts:959/:1076), so the tempting source when T-011 writes one is PINNED_CCUSAGE_VERSION (src/resolve-ccusage.ts:21) — the version that SHIPS, not the one that RAN, because CCUSAGE_CMD overrides the executable (src/context.ts:192). That is this project's defect class (b) one field over. It is not a blocker: requireString refuses only the empty string, so a truthful non-claim is representable, and a real witness exists in the resolved binary's own --version self-report. T-011's acceptanceAdditions now binds it to record what the resolved binary reports, never the build-time constant.

Closed with the verification attached rather than silently, because a high-severity issue left open over a landed fix is exactly the bookkeeping lag a later session re-reads as a live blocker.
